name: desire for privacy
description: A desire to avoid unnecessary social attention at the moment.
perceptions: Being very social seems unimportant or unappealing right now.

guidance.description: It's ok if you get a social invitation that you want to decline.

comparisons.description: Being around your noisy family may still be considered being private. Likewise, a quiet public library may still feel exposing if you're not feeling well.

variations.name: desire for social rest
variations.description: Social withdrawal driven by a simple need for some downtime. Depending your personality, this may be infrequent or often.
perceptions: A social interaction may cost more energy than I have right now.

variations.name: desire for social recovery
variations.description: Social withdrawal after negative social experience like anxiety, cynicism, shame, ennui, or contempt.
perceptions: After what happened, I need a break from that group.

variations.name: limit what others know about you
variations.description: Desire to keep certain information from certain people. Some people live their lives on social media, others prefer a smaller circle.
perceptions: Concern about what someone may do with a particular piece of information.
Concern about how someone might perceive you if they had this detail.

commentaries.quote: It can be hard for us to balance being an individual integrated as part of several groups, some of which we may not be fully aligned with. We like to have a sense of safety and control, and we may sometimes perceive that a social situation causes as much anxiety as joy.
My take is, privacy is precious. I think privacy is the last true luxury. To be able to live your life as you choose without having everyone comment on it or know about.
When it comes to privacy and accountability, people always demand the former for themselves and the latter for everyone else.
But there are other words for privacy and independence. They are isolation and loneliness.
commentaries.attribution: Megan Whalen Turner in 'The King of Attolia'

commentaries.quote: I don't know why people are so keen to put the details of their private life in public; they forget that invisibility is a superpower.

names: limit what others know about you
